items.gist: Devas stationed in their proper functions grant fruit when worshipped; avatars and devotees are described in this context.
Beings dying in the dvaya attain sālokyam through karma and lack of discrimination; the passage then turns to measuring sacred fields in towns.
The fruit of a liṅga depends on whether it is installed by a tattvavit or not; only the tattvavit's installation is supreme.
A shrine is taken refuge in for bhukti and mukti; the yogin's path and the use of kṣetra are distinguished.
Initiated beings attain proximity to their deity according to fitness; those who die in higher tattvas attain union with Rudra.
Avatāras vary in splendor according to karma and enjoyment; initiates at different tattva levels receive corresponding results.
Sālokya, sāmīpya, and sāyujya are distinguished for animals, initiates, and higher beings; the yogin transcends ordinary death.
Those who cling to lower shrines near death are affected by knowledge-defilement; defilers of knowledge, shrine, and initiation go to hell.
Saṃskāras are burned by knowledge; kaivalya-oriented saṃskāras arise through śaktipāta and are not ordinary rebirth tendencies.
Tirobhāva is not recognized in the heart; even the awakened experience bodily results of karma without losing liberation.
Yogins who leave the body through dhāraṇā enter another body without confusion; there is no delusion for those moving through tattva-bodies.
